memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: Review of insomnia, anxiety and NAFLD management.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports difficulty falling asleep, waking 2-3 times nightly, daytime fatigue, and occasional worry about work. Denies chest pain or palpitations.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/84 mmHg, pulse 78/min, weight 58 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 24.1 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. No focal neurological deficits.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia moderate, GAD stable, NAFLD suspected. Advise weight reduction, sleep hygiene. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting glucose, TSH, Hb, LFT.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start melatonin 3 mg HS, trazodone 50 mg HS, escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD, silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Return if new chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or bleeding per rectum.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: Follow‑up on sleep, anxiety and liver labs.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Sleep slightly better, still wakes once; anxiety less intense but reports muscle tension. No new pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80, weight 57.5 kg, BMI 23.9 (overweight). Abdomen soft, liver edge not palpable.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia improving, GAD mild, LFT shows mild ALT rise. Continue current meds, recheck labs in 3 months.
ARRANGEMENTS: Keep melatonin 3 mg HS, trazodone 50 mg HS, escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD, silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Return if worsening insomnia, panic attacks, jaundice, or abdominal swelling.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: Autumn review; assess NAFLD and vaccine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports improved sleep, only occasional early awakening. Anxiety low, occasional worry about finances. No chest pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/82, weight 57 kg, BMI 23.7 (overweight). Abdomen soft, liver edge just palpable.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia mild, GAD well‑controlled, NAFLD likely. Need abdominal ultrasound to assess steatosis. Offer influenza vaccine.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Order abdominal ultrasound. Give influenza vaccine today (02‑Oct‑2025). Return if fever >39°C, dyspnoea, worsening jaundice, or melena.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Abdominal ultrasound: Liver shows diffuse increased echogenicity consistent with steatosis. Spleen normal, no focal lesion, portal vein patent. No ascites.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to Dr. S. Rao, Gastroenterology, for further evaluation of NAFLD and possible fibrosis scoring.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Gastroenterology review: Ultrasound confirms steatosis. Fibroscan shows CAP 260 dB/m, E‑fibrosis 6.2 kPa (F1). Recommend lifestyle modification, continue rosuvastatin, repeat LFT in 6 months. No hepatotoxic drugs advised.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: Post‑holiday check; review trazodone side‑effects.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes daytime grogginess after trazodone, feels ‘hangover’. Sleep onset improved, still wakes once. Anxiety stable.
EXAMINATION: BP 129/81, weight 56.8 kg, BMI 23.6 (overweight). No neurological deficits.
IMPRESSION: Trazodone causing morning sedation; consider taper. Insomnia mild, GAD controlled, NAFLD stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Taper trazodone to 25 mg HS for two weeks then stop. Continue melatonin 3 mg HS, escitalopram 10 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD, silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Return if worsening insomnia, anxiety spikes, or abdominal pain.

Reason: Routine follow‑up; assess lipid and liver.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports good sleep, no daytime sedation. Anxiety low, occasional worry. No abdominal discomfort.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80, weight 56.5 kg, BMI 23.5 (overweight). Abdomen soft, liver edge not palpable.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia resolved, GAD in remission, LDL improved on statin, LFT stable. Continue preventive meds.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue melatonin 3 mg HS, escitalopram 10 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD, silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Order fasting lipid profile, LFT, TSH, Hb. Return if new chest pain, dyspnoea, jaundice, or melena.

Reason: Annual review; influenza vaccine and chronic disease check.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports sleeping well, feels rested. Anxiety absent, occasional mild worry about grandchildren. No abdominal pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 127/78, weight 56 kg, BMI 23.3 (overweight). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Insomnia in remission, GAD well‑controlled, NAFLD stable, lipids at goal. Vaccinated against influenza.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue melatonin 3 mg HS, escitalopram 10 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD, silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Influenza vaccine given today (05‑Oct‑2026). Return if fever >39°C, dyspnoea, jaundice, or melena.
